title: Cream a forearm wound with an applicator, then put on a fabric plaster by its liner tabs, never touching pad or adhesive
instruction: Apply the antiseptic cream to the wound on the practice forearm and the marked margin around it with the applicator, without double-dipping, and throw the applicator away. Then put the plaster on with its pad centred over the creamed wound, lengthwise along the arm, and press it down. Don't touch the wound, the pad or the adhesive, keep cream off the adhesive, and throw the liners away.
context: Dressing minor wounds is a core O*NET task of medical assistants (31-9092.00 #2035 'Change dressings on wounds'; 833,900 jobs, BLS 2025) and LPNs (29-2061.00 #511 '...dressing wounds...'; 666,900); nursing assistants (31-1131.00 #19318) and EMTs (29-2042.00 #22852 first aid) do it too. A smeared or double-dipped applicator, cream under the adhesive, a touched pad or an unstuck wing means another dressing change. A liner pulled low along the strip peels from under the wing; pulled steeply it lifts the wing; with nothing holding the strip, the pull drags it off the wound. The wings stick only where pressed.
setup: Metres from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left, z up from the table. Nasco Life/form Suture and Stapling Practice Arm LF01028 (vinyl over foam) lies across the table, palm down, hand toward +y, axis at x 0.30, top 75 mm up, strapped to a 180 x 470 x 6 mm plywood base at (0.30, 0.065) under an underpad. Wound: 14 x 7 mm abrasion painted with moulage paint at (0.30, 0.00), long axis along the arm, with a dotted blue skin-marker outline 5 mm out from its edge. Cream: 0.5 mL 10% povidone-iodine ointment (brown) as a dollop in a 30 mL medicine cup on a 70 x 70 x 25 mm HDPE block at (0.30, -0.205). Applicator: sterile 6 in (152 mm) wooden cotton-tipped applicator (Puritan 806-WC), bud 5 mm, in its peel pouch opened at the handle end, on a 130 x 60 x 25 mm HDPE tray at (0.16, -0.17), lying along x, bud toward the robot, handle 50 mm out past the tray's far edge. Plaster: Band-Aid Flexible Fabric Extra Large 1.75 x 4 in (44 x 102 mm), re-lined (reset notes) with two C-folded release liners whose tabs stick out 25 mm past each end, lying along y on its opened wrapper on a 70 x 80 x 35 mm HDPE riser at (0.44, 0.00). Waste pot: 1 L open bin, 110 mm across and high, at (0.15, 0.02). Disposable finger-cot covers on the fingertip pads, marked with Glo Germ UV gel over a lined tray. A clear 10 x 12 cm film dressing (3M Tegaderm 1626W) over the wound site, renewed each trial, keeps the iodine off the vinyl; four marker ticks on it, 60 mm along and 30 mm round the arm from the wound's centre. A phone on a stand looks down on the wound.
scoring: Overhead video, ruler, film ticks, 1 mm grid, 0.25 mm feeler, UV torch. 1.0 when, held 1 s: brown film on >=90% of the outline (grid, frame after binning), no smear over 2 x 2 mm >3 mm past it, applicator in the pot; pad centre <=4 mm from the wound's, strip <=10 deg off the arm (ticks); liners in the pot, feeler under no wing edge; fingers >=3 cm from the plaster. 0.75: cream done, pad over the outline, both liners off, a wing stuck full length. 0.5: cream done, pad over the outline, a liner off, its wing stuck full length. 0.25: cream done. 75-90% film, no smear, applicator binned or unused: 0.5 if the plaster meets 0.5+; under 75%: 0.25 if it meets 1.0. 0 if a gripper touches the bare wound, pad face or adhesive; ointment under the adhesive; a re-dip after skin, or the bud touching anything but cream and skin (cup rim, plaster, gripper, table; pot while held); or the plaster falls.
reset_notes: Per trial: a fresh applicator, cup and 0.5 mL of ointment, and a plaster re-lined with end-tab liners (about 60 s, gloved, touching only paper and the plaster's back): fold two 44 x 127 mm strips of siliconised label backing 51 mm from one end, silicone out; peel one stock liner, lay that half's adhesive on a strip's short leaf, fold at the pad's middle, long leaf 25 mm past the end; repeat. The tabs give the hold-by-the-strips, place, pull-away sequence of first-aid guidance (HSE Ireland) and of two-half-backed dressings (Smith & Nephew PRIMAPORE). Peel the used plaster low and slow, check the adhesive for ointment and UV marker, renew the clear film over the site (and the moulage and outline under it if faded), fit fresh finger-cot covers marked with Glo Germ gel (not powder) over a tray, UV-check the rig before and after and lay the parts on their outlines.
fidelity: Reduced model (README). Applicator and liner tabs: loose PhysX bodies held only by friction (both pads >=1 N); tabs hinged at roots until held. Ointment: 0.5 mm height field. Plaster: 35 x 9 nodes. Liner peel resists the tab as a native PhysX force, 0.27 N (0.43 N start peak; siliconised liner, 0.15 N/25 mm at 180 deg); the same force drags the strip unless skin friction, pressed pads, tack or the other held tab hold it. Tack only under a pad pressing >=1 N. No wrinkles or rate effects.
